claims.text: OrdersController.Create has one unconditional return, CreatedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id = order.Id }, ToDto(order)); it never branches on whether anything already exists.

RFC 9110 §9.3.3: when a POST successfully creates one or more resources, the origin server SHOULD send a 201 (Created) response containing a Location header field identifying the primary resource created.
RFC 9110 §9.2.2 lists PUT, DELETE, and the safe methods as idempotent; POST is not among them, so repeating an identical POST is not guaranteed to have the same effect as sending it once.
CreateOrderRequest (DonHang.Api/Dtos.cs) has exactly one property, Items; it has no field for an id, so a client cannot put one in the request body.

ASP.NET Core's CreatedAtAction builds the Location header from the named action's own route (here, Get's [HttpGet("{id:int}")] under the controller's [Route("api/v1/orders")]), filled in with the route values passed to it (here, the new order's id).
[Authorize] on Create means a request with no valid signed-in credentials never reaches the method body; customerId inside Create comes from who is signed in, never from the request JSON.
